title: How Does a Fridge Work?
short_title: Your Fridge Doesn't Make Cold... It Moves Heat
description: A fridge doesn't make cold, it moves heat out of the box into your room. Here is the simple science: evaporation, compression, condensation and expansion.
comment: Did you know the back of your fridge is warm? Which everyday thing should Professor Alienstein explain next?

scenes.text: Your fridge does not make cold. It moves heat. Mind blown?
Inside the fridge, a special liquid called refrigerant evaporates into gas. Evaporating soaks up heat, just like sweat cools your skin.
Then the compressor squeezes that gas. Squeezing makes it super hot, hotter than your kitchen. Like pumping a bike tyre: the pump gets hot!
Hot coils at the back release that heat into your room. The gas cools and turns back into liquid.
Then a tiny tube drops the pressure, the liquid turns icy cold, and the loop starts again.
So keep the back clear and don't leave the door open. Your fridge is not an air conditioner!
